findings.claim: Reading a legacy-layout complex obs still costs 6 filesystem operations with 3 Files.exists calls (plus a failed stat), the same total as master. So TRUNK-6682's 'at most one existence-related check' acceptance criterion, and the PR description's unqualified '3 filesystem operations' claim, hold only for new-layout obs. Does the ticket stay open for legacy obs, or is its criterion narrowed? This belongs as a reply in the still-unanswered thread 4070873940, which asked the same scope question when the new-layout path was still at 5 operations.
findings.evidence: I wrote a throwaway BaseContextSensitiveTest that counts static Files.exists/readAttributes/newInputStream calls with Mockito.mockStatic(CALLS_REAL_METHODS). It drives AbstractHandler.getObs, TextHandler RAW_VIEW and BinaryDataHandler RAW_VIEW on a new-layout obs saved through the handler, and on a legacy obs ('t.txt|legacy_<uuid>.txt' with the file at <appdata>/obs/). Results: PR head new layout exists=1 readAttributes=1 newInputStream=1 (3 ops, matching the PR's claim, which serves as the known-good control); PR head legacy exists=3 readAttributes=2 newInputStream=1 (6 ops); master both layouts exists=4 readAttributes=1 newInputStream=1 (6 ops). Where the 3 come from: parseDataKey -> LocalStorageService.exists probes the current path and then <appdata>/<raw key> (LocalStorageService.java:286). read() then fails a stat on the current path and probes the legacy path (LocalStorageService.java:109). No count test covers the legacy path; all call-count tests use keys saved in the new layout. The test file was deleted afterwards.

findings.claim: TRUNK-6682 carries the 'backport' label, but the new API is tagged @since 3.0.0 only, with no maintenance-line versions (StorageService/LocalStorageService list '2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15'). The main code also uses Java 16+ syntax: the private record LoadedImage at ImageHandler.java:153 and pattern-matching instanceof at S3StorageService.java:178. A cherry-pick onto the 2.x lines therefore won't compile. This is the surviving sub-point of thread 4070873955, which asked for the version this lands in 'plus whatever maintenance lines it gets backported to'. Only the first half was addressed.
findings.evidence: Ticket snapshot labels: backport, community-priority, performance. `git show a085b50b6^:pom.xml` (the commit just before 'Bump version to 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT', i.e. the 2.8.x line's content) has <javaCompilerVersion>1.8</javaCompilerVersion>. `javac --release 8` on a snippet with a private record and `instanceof X x` fails with 'records are not supported in -source 8' and 'pattern matching in instanceof is not supported in -source 8'; the same snippet compiles with --release 21. `grep @since` on the storage package shows the multi-version precedent. I could not see the maintenance branches themselves (the clone holds only master's history), so the current Java level of 2.8.x is inferred from the pre-3.0 pom.

verdict: Close to mergeable on master: the new-layout read path now does 1 exists + 1 stat + 1 open (down from 6), and every prior review thread except two is resolved and covered by tests that go red under mutation. What's still open is scope, not correctness: legacy-layout obs still cost 6 operations with 3 existence checks, so the ticket's 'at most one' criterion is met only for new-layout data, and a maintainer needs to decide whether TRUNK-6682 stays open for that (plus how the backport will be done).
what_i_swept: Pass 1 (approach and solution fit): I checked the diff stat (21 files, +967/-68, identical for two-dot and three-dot, so no drift), the PR body, the TRUNK-6682 snapshot and all 31 inline comments, 11 reviews and 13 PR comments. I verified each prior thread against the head: formatting, the getData/getMetadata internal split and the metadata-before-data comment, NoSuchFileException documented on StorageService, the default interface method for module implementations, the S3 multipart length via Content-Range plus a mocked-client test, the FileSystemException fallback for over-long legacy names and its test directory, the exists() containment check, handler-level count tests for all five handlers, the ImageHandler legacy title fallback, the obsDir guard removed, the deprecated 2-arg injectMissingMetadata, the restored AbstractHandler count test, and the legacy getDataWithMetadata test. I measured real filesystem I/O per read on master and on the PR for both key layouts. Pass 2 (outward trace): I checked callers of getPath (only purgeData, so the Javadoc claim holds), other StorageService implementations (Local, S3, test CountingStorageService), every caller of exists/getDataWithMetadata/injectMissingMetadata, and the switch from legacy-first to current-first precedence between read() and purgeData's getPath (judged unreachable in practice because encodeKey escapes dots, so no finding). I also checked handler exception-behaviour changes (missing file still ends in IllegalArgumentException from Assert.notNull; other IOExceptions now become APIException), stream closing on every handler path, S3 404 translation, and containment/traversal in read() and exists(). Pass 3: I mutation-tested the tests and ran the S3 IT; nothing new surfaced.
could_not_verify: The Java level of the current 2.x maintenance branches: the clone has only master's history, so 'Java 8' is inferred from the pom just before the 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT bump (a085b50b6^).
